summary: Pupils at a lycée in Créteil, outside Paris, began protesting in mid-September 2026 over dilapidated buildings and teacher shortages, and school blockades spread nationwide.

On 6 October authorities counted about a quarter of a million marchers; the high school students’ union said nearly 2,000 schools were blockaded or closed, and the prime minister suspended high school classes for the rest of the week.
On 17 October the protests joined a broader day of action over living costs, with clashes and looting in several cities.

detained.n: Placed in police custody (garde à vue) from the start of the movement to 8 Oct, 86% of them minors, per the Justice Ministry.

Mostly peaceful, with clashes in Lyon and other cities.
Education strike: students blockade dozens of high schools (49 of about 3,700 by mid-morning, per the ministry). Unions call a new day of action for 17 November.

Third united public-sector strike day, joined by high school and university students. Interior Ministry: 146,000 marchers, 28,000 of them in Paris; the CGT union said just over 500,000. Described as largely peaceful; no arrests or injuries reported.

grievances: $4 million for new cars for 65 MPs
summary: More than 1,000 mostly university students rallied near Parliament against a plan to spend $4 million on cars for each of the 65 MPs.
Within days MPs dropped the car plan and agreed to scrap lifetime pensions, passed into law on 26 September.

4: More than 1,000 students on 15 Sep; about 2,000 on 16 Sep.

injured.n: Protesters hurt by tear gas on 15 Sep.

detained.n: A widely repeated figure of 22 arrests refers to a 2018 protest, not 2025.

timeline: Students arrested for protesting a $1 million car purchase for MPs.
Plan approved to allocate $4 million for MPs’ cars.
Protests; car plan dropped; pensions to be scrapped.
Parliament votes unanimously to end lifetime pensions.

movements.statusWhy: The prime minister was removed, but early signs pointed to continuity rather than reform.
grievances: The prime minister’s family’s lavish lifestyle
summary: Peaceful youth-led protests in Sukhbaatar Square followed viral posts about the prime minister’s son’s lavish lifestyle.
A petition gathered more than 59,000 signatures, and on 3 June 2025 the prime minister resigned after losing a confidence vote.

1: Viral social media posts about the PM’s family sparked the protests.
3: Peaceful sit-in protests in Sukhbaatar Square; a petition with 59,000+ signatures.
5: The prime minister lost a confidence vote and resigned.

timeline: Oyun-Erdene becomes prime minister after protests force his predecessor out.
PM resigns after losing a confidence vote.
Parliament confirms a new prime minister.
